matches.quote: T_c rises wherever R_s rises and μ falls. Under illumination μ rises and T_c falls. ... Plot T_c against μ, R_s and n for all states
The link between the dielectric-loss peaks and the 2DEG phenomena is qualitative ... Either provide a model ... or soften the "coincidence" argument.
T_c may simply track the normal-state transport, independent of PNR-mediated pairing. ... Plot T_c against μ, R_s and n for all states
The PNR "internal gating" and remnant polarization are inferred, not measured. ... Measure ε and tan δ directly in the programmed states
Integrate I_g and compare the transferred charge with the Hall Δn·e·A and with C·ΔV.
Sample statistics are limited. Everything appears to come from one 2.5 × 2.5 mm device. ... Show device-to-device spread.
Any trapping hysteresis proportional to the induced charge gives Δ_L ∝ ε without invoking OV ionization physics.
So the LED, 1 cm above the sample, does heat the sample. ... Report the on-sample temperature during illumination.
Error bars are missing on T_c, E_a, τ, ΔR/R₁ and Δ_L throughout.
Illumination has "no obvious change" at 2 K but a strong effect at 10–15 K. A 1.97 eV photon excitation ... should not depend on whether the lattice is at 2 or 10 K.
If the points collapse onto a single curve, the T_c memory is a by-product of the normal-state memory. The PNR-pairing claim would then be unsupported.
H_c2 or I–V data for pristine, cycled and illuminated states would strengthen the claim that the superconducting state itself, not only the percolation path, is programmed.
Unipolar (negative-only and positive-only) cycles. ... Supp. Fig. 3 is measured after illumination with a "+ first" sequence, whereas Fig. 1 starts from the pristine state with "− first".
Report retention ... for both the programmed and the illuminated states. ... An activated process with E_a = 76 meV would change its rate by many orders of magnitude
Report retention at base temperature (hours to days) for both the programmed and the illuminated states.
Give uncertainties on T_p and E_a. The Peak 2 Arrhenius points in Fig. 3c appear curved.
Fig. 2i compares only L0–L4 and does not overlay the pristine (never-gated) transition. ... Present pristine, cycled and illuminated (L4) values of R_s, n, μ and T_c
Show power and wavelength dependence. If the effect is optical, it should scale with photon dose and follow a defect absorption threshold.
Assess the phase error from series resistance (R_s ~ 1 kΩ, C ~ 200 pF), cabling and lock-in phase at 4 kHz.
Extract P–E loops from integrated I_g. ... PNR internal gating should change n differently for the two sweep directions.

notes: C10 asks for both retention time and 100-1000 cycle endurance; P20 directly raises retention time of the programmed state. C4 asks for direct probes (PFM/STEM/XPS) while P21/P13 ask for direct polarization and dielectric controls, so C4 is judged 'partly'. C5 asks about overdoping on the superconducting dome; P12 asks to plot Tc against n and mobility to test if normal-state transport explains Tc without PNRs, so C5 is judged 'partly'.
